author: reek
body: Build playable decks from a real bridged card pool. The imported pool has no basic lands (and singletons only), so we append the five basics as templates and fill a mono-color deck with a basic-land mana base plus creatures of that color cycled to the requested spell count. This makes real Old School cards playable by the existing Simulate AI.

author: reek
body: Append the five basics after the bridged templates. Their ids are the pool size plus a fixed color offset, so basic-land-id can recover them.

author: reek
body: A draftable "spell" is a coloured Instant or Sorcery with real (non-inert) behaviour. Enchantments are drafted by their own colour package (see below), NOT mixed into this -cmc ranking -- mixing them made anthems compete with (and lose to) cheap removal, and re-ranking the whole spell base by role mis-valued the symmetric sweepers (Hurricane/Earthquake) that hurt a creature deck. Artifacts are colourless and drafted by the mana-rock and utility-artifact packages. So this pick stays exactly the tuned Instant/Sorcery base it always was.

author: reek
body: fill-copies never wraps: once every distinct id has its per-card allotment the fill stops, even if slots remain. Wrapping handed out a fresh four-of per pass, so a thin pool built 6+ copies of one card -- an illegal deck the gauntlet then scored. Callers pad any shortfall with basic lands to hold the 60-card total.

author: reek
body: Utility artifacts (Icy Manipulator, Nevinyrral's Disk, Jayemdae Tome, Rod of Ruin, ...) are the colourless backbone of Old School alongside the mana rocks. Like the rock package they are singletons drafted as a small fixed package (colourless -> not reachable by the colour spell pick, and computing them inside the builder avoids any main/splash double-draft). Only non-mana artifacts with a real ACTIVATED ability qualify -- the AI actively fires those via ai-activate-taps, so they are unambiguously useful with no symmetric-static evaluation guesswork. They replace that many spell slots (they ARE the deck's noncreature spells), and the cap is archetype-aware: an aggressive deck takes at most one four-drop artifact, a controlling deck up to three, so curves stay honest.

author: reek
body: Utility artifacts are ranked by their fit for the archetype. An artifact with an activated ability the AI actively fires (Icy / Disk / Tome / Rod) is a universal premium; the static globals split by archetype -- opponent-punishers (Black Vise, Ankh) reward an aggressive deck racing the opponent's hand and land drops, while the lock pieces (Winter Orb, Stasis, Meekstone) reward a controlling deck built to sit under them. Self-harmful statics (Copper Tablet, Power Surge) are excluded above. The best-fit artifacts fill the small archetype-capped package.

author: reek
body: The enchantment package gives the deck's coloured non-Aura enchantments (anthems like Crusade / Bad Moon, the Circles of Protection, Karma, and the continuous global enchantments) their own dedicated slots, kept OUT of the -cmc spell ranking so they never crowd out removal. It is small and archetype-aware -- an aggressive deck runs a couple (an anthem is worth it to a go-wide board), a control deck a few more -- and takes multiple copies of the best (pool-order, which fronts the premier anthems) so an anthem plays as a real 2-of, not a singleton. Verified to hold format health against the FormatSolver baseline.

author: reek
body: A two-colour (splash) deck. Mostly the main colour, with a handful of off-colour spells and a mana base that can cast them: the main-colour rock package, up to four dual lands making both colours, three splash-colour basics, and the rest main-colour basics -- the total land slot count is unchanged, so the deck is still 60 cards. The spell slots are split into the main spells and up to splash-budget off-colour spells (the best of each by the same value ranking).
